_doc: THE DERIVED RESEARCH LAYER, AND THE COMMAND THAT REBUILDS EACH PART OF IT. Read by tools/rederive.mjs, which .github/steward/pr-lap.sh calls when a merge conflicts. WHY THIS EXISTS (owner, 2026-09-10): with the lap finally able to merge at all (PR #1058), every remaining open PR was left alone for a REAL CONFLICT, and every conflicting file was a tool output two runs had each re-derived — directory crosswalks, the land-sale spend, identity_master. pr-lap.sh already draws exactly the right line for this: 'A conflict here is never resolved by hand: the merge takes either side to clear the marker and the tool then rewrites the file from source.' It just drew it around five bookkeeping files. This file widens it, EXPLICITLY, so the widening is auditable rather than a glob nobody can audit.
_the_rule: A path under `resolves` may have its conflict cleared by taking either side, because a step below rewrites it from its inputs. A path NOT listed here is refused exactly as before — that is the whole safety property, and it is why this file enumerates rather than pattern-matches. `resolves: []` means the step runs to keep the tree consistent but resolves no conflict: its outputs are still content a run may have meant to change.
_the_backstop: Nothing here is trusted on its say-so. After the sequence runs, tools/check.sh must pass, and it is check.sh that asserts each of these files re-derives from its inputs. A wrong entry here makes the gate RED, and pr-lap.sh does not push a red tree. The failure mode is a PR that stays open — the one it was already in — never a bad merge onto dev.
_only_gated_tools: A step may only appear here if tools/check.sh runs its tool with --check. That invariant is enforced by rederive.mjs --check, and it is not decoration — it is the whole reason the backstop above is real. Learned by nearly shipping the opposite: crosswalk_norris_1844_advertiser.py was in this file on first draft, and running it rebuilt norris_1844_advertiser_crosswalk_1835.json from 443 lines to 195, taking data/residents/directories.json down with it. check.sh does not invoke that tool AT ALL, so nothing in the gate would have gone red and the lap would have pushed the loss. An ungated derivation is one whose committed file nobody has ever asserted re-derives, and this file may not resolve a conflict by re-running one.
_never: A file declaring `hand_authored: true` is refused even if listed. data/research/land_sales/resident_rulings.json is the one such file today: a judgement is not a derivation, and re-running a tool over it would erase the argument. rederive.mjs --check fails if any listed path declares it.

steps.why: The directory crosswalks: each reads its own transcribed claims file and adjudicates it against the residents layer. Two runs that both touch the residents layer both re-derive all of these, which is why they conflict so readily.

The church rolls, rebuilt from their transcribed records. T-0962 found second_presbyterian's 83 matched rows this morning; the count moves whenever the town gains a card the roll reaches, which is exactly the kind of drift two slices produce.
The land-sale crosswalk folds resident_rulings.json — HAND-AUTHORED, and refused above — onto the deposit. The crosswalk is a derivation of the two; the rulings are not.
The spends run AFTER their crosswalks, because a spend reads the crosswalk it is spending.
The obituary crosswalk: the old-settlers death notices adjudicated against the residents layer, on the same footing as the directory crosswalks above.
The Newberry genealogical index and the leads it proposes.
The 1835 business register, compiled from the newspaper corpus.
The resident-research synthesis, downstream of the crosswalks and read by the ladder.
The cross-domain consolidation reads every crosswalk above, so it runs after all of them.

REBUILD ONLY, resolves nothing — and the ordering here was learned the hard way on PR #1055. mint_civic_residents writes 486 resident CARDS from the ladder, and consolidate moves the inputs it reads: built before consolidate it still differed on two cards, and only converged when re-run after it. Its outputs are resident cards, which a run may have meant to change by hand, so a conflict in one is never cleared by this file.

The duplicate-cluster ledger, rebuilt from the town and the merge rulings — it runs after mint because it reads the cards mint writes. `--candidates` and NOT `--apply`: --apply performs the card merges and rewrites resident cards (tested on a clean dev, it modified hh_kinzie_john_h.json), which is a judgement being carried out and never something a merge resolution may do on its own. --candidates writes this one ledger and nothing else. Added after the first real use of this manifest left check.sh red on `town_card_candidates.json does not re-derive`.
The ladder's spend, which reads the consolidated evidence above it.
The liberties register, compiled from the sidecars and the town — every liberty the reconstruction takes, with its reason.
The scene compiles from the residents layer, so it runs last but one.
The final audit package re-derives from the residents layer and is the last thing downstream of all of it.
